text:
zoe: Heads up — my internet decided to become a performance art project mid-demo. router is now on a bookshelf next to a ficus. :seedling:

liam: oh no. bookshelf routing is a new strategy. did it improve signal or aesthetics?

zoe: aesthetics up 100%, throughput not so much. presentations turned into a slide show of my forehead. :sweat_smile:

anya: pop quiz: are you on apartment fiber or cable? some cables get noisy at dinner time.

zoe: cable. spectrum or similar. speedtest says download 12 Mbps but upload is 0.9.

frazer: brutal. if you've got symmetrical requirements for calls, cable can be a pain. tether to phone as fallback if the demo is critical.

it-bot: [automated] If you file an IT ticket, attach `~/connectivity.log` and a screenshot of the speedtest. See IT KB: https://intra.redwood/it/connectivity 

liam: for logs I like this tiny one-liner: `while sleep 30; do date -Is; ping -c1 1.1.1.1 | awk -F'=' '{print $NF}'; done >> ~/net-spike.log`

anya: also try an Ethernet run if possible. My wife got an ethernet patch cable and a little USB-C -> ethernet adapter and it solved morning chaos.

zoe: no ethernet near the shelf. tempted to roll the whole desk downstairs to the living room where the modem sits. moving furniture mid-meeting is a flex.

frazer: do it. dramatic entrance: "sorry, I'm relocating my office for better latency." :laughing:

liam: vote: who else has a router in an embarrassing spot? share pics. new channel suggestion: #home-office-oddities

anya: YES. I'll start with my router in the closet because "out of sight, out of mind". surprisingly works.

zoe: fine. uploading mine in a sec (pls lowercase my forehead).

zoe: https://img.example.com/bookshelf-router-321.jpg

liam: iconic. 10/10 for aesthetic bravery.

it-bot: [automated] Notice: Someone reported intermittent home internet. IT will triage if a ticket is created.

anya: practical note: check your coax splitter if you have cable TV + internet. splitters can degrade signal over time. My tech swapped mine and my upload jumped.

zoe: didn't know splitters could be gremlins. adding to checklist.

frazer: if you end up filing with ISP, escalate to tier 2 if tech says "we see no issue" but your logs disagree. they sometimes need the word "intermittent" and attached logs.

zoe: thanks team. starting the log now and debating rolling the desk. will report back with either triumph or tragic furniture injury.

liam: good luck. if you need a spare mesh node we have an office stash — ping me.

zoe: saving that like it's a golden ticket. :sparkles:

(zoe pinned message: "net-spike.log")
